questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. You must take extra steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance when driving near a cyclist.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful around cyclists. Always keep a safe distance between your vehicle and the cyclist.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate comes down.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not pay attention to how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue driving until you reach the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Drive to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway is illegal.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Take the next exit.
Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Wave down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss your exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give that vehicle extra space.
Understand that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not copy the driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers are more likely to have accidents. Keep extra space between you and them. Do not become distracted yourself.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm out. Wait until the arm is pulled back before you drive.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Look directly at the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up—this makes them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra time for your trip.
Obey the speed limit.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey the speed limit, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful near children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Keep driving and use the next exit.
Back up to return to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn at your exit. If you miss it, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand in traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs have black letters or symbols on a yellow background. Work zone warning signs have black letters or symbols on an orange background.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no train in sight or sound. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is down.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a stop sign, a flagger, or a train. If you are unsure if it is safe to cross, stop. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Driving involves risk, so it is important to always improve your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe if you think you have nothing to improve. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they cannot change your BAC.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Move your eyes around to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one spot for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in your current direction.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never go around the gate.

questions.question: What is a good way to prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and take a nap, or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, even if the crossing guard gives different instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards, signs, and police officers in school zones. Slow down and use extra caution when directed by a crossing guard.
